title: MZ Change Face Image When Hit In Battle Plugin ?

posts.author: Etrogade_
posts.body:
So, I've looked for a while as to how to make this. I've tried Waynee95's CustomFaceImageEval's along with several forum posts but they always end up the same or somewhere close to the same. When trying to replicate it, the effect is usually the face changing but it's not every time the actor gets hit, the actor's face stays when getting hit and doesn't change, or it doesn't change at all
I decided to try Hakuen Studio's Face Reaction, but all I get back is error messages. Even after uploading it to a completely new project it still messes up.
I've even tried Yanfly's Buffs and States Core to change the faces, but it didn't work. AND I've tried Yanfly's Base Troops Events combined with a event that changes the actor's face when the state is applied, but still, nothing.
I've nearly given up on trying to add this feature to the game, but I would like to know if there is
some
way I could do it.
Through states or straight up scripts, if it works, I'm fine.

I don't know what is the configuration you have for Visustella, but since I fixed some compatibility issues with their plugins these days, I had a project already set up, so I did a little test with my Faces Reaction and it worked fine with Battle Core. I mean, no error. And that error you got must show up regardless the plugin parameter or the face images you set.
The error you are getting seems to be that the
Game_Actor
did not properly initiate the object
_faceReactionData
, so it is
undefined
. The only thing I can think that could happened is if the
initMembers
method has been overwriten.
Since Visustella plugins are obfuscated and plus some statements of their terms of use, I cannot guarantee for sure that I will manage to make a patch to fix that or even find the problem. But I already got lucky this week two times, so, upload this project you have somewhere and send me the link of it on PM here on the forums. That is the best way for me to take a look and find/fix the problem.

Okay! So I found out what the problem was!
The normal face sheet that's provided by RPG Maker is 144x144.
However,
the face sheet I'm using contains faces of 192x164. Because of the sizes of the faces, it messes up how the plugin is supposed to perceive the png.
Because of this, I'd have to go into the plugin code to change the face size limit or something like that.
